input: The performance of a mechanical-draft cooling tower at a chemical site was logged over the course of one summer month. The mean wet-bulb temperature recorded over the month was 23 °C. The approach was 7 K, which means that the cold water left the tower at 30 °C, and the range was 8 K, which means that the water entered the tower at 38 °C. It should be noted that the approach is defined as the difference between the leaving cold-water temperature and the wet-bulb temperature, while the range is the fall in water temperature across the tower, so the two figures together place the tower's water temperatures against the air condition prevailing during the logged month. A wet-bulb temperature, it may be explained, is the temperature that the air reaches when water is evaporated into it to saturation, and it sets the lowest temperature to which the tower is able to cool its water. The two water temperatures are the temperatures that the tower actually received and delivered during the month, and they are the figures that a user of the log would take for the duty that the tower performed over that period. A mechanical-draft tower moves air by means of a fan, and its performance follows the wet-bulb temperature of the entering air. It is important to emphasise, however, that performance outside the logged month was not measured. In particular, performance at winter wet-bulb temperatures is not established by this log, and the summer approach and range cannot simply be carried over and assumed to apply to winter operation.
target: Performance of a mechanical-draft cooling tower at a chemical site was logged over one summer month. The mean wet-bulb temperature over the month was 23 °C. With an approach of 7 K, the cold water left the tower at 30 °C; with a range of 8 K, the water entered the tower at 38 °C. The approach is the difference between the leaving cold-water temperature and the wet-bulb temperature, and the range is the fall in water temperature across the tower, so the two figures place the tower's water temperatures against the air condition of the logged month. A wet-bulb temperature is the temperature the air reaches when water evaporates into it to saturation, and it sets the lowest temperature to which the tower can cool its water. The two water temperatures are the temperatures the tower actually received and delivered during the month, and they are the figures a user of the log takes for the duty the tower performed. A mechanical-draft tower moves air with a fan, and its performance follows the wet-bulb temperature of the entering air. Performance outside the logged month was not measured. Performance at winter wet-bulb temperatures in particular is not established by this log, and the summer approach and range are not transferable to winter operation. Any judgement about the tower in another season needs measurements taken in that season.
